sources.entry: gSwitch - macOS status bar app that allows control over the gpu on dual gpu macbooks.

summary.one_liner: gSwitch is a macOS menu bar app for dual-GPU MacBook Pros that lets you choose integrated, discrete, or dynamic graphics switching; the project is now archived.
summary.what_it_does: The app puts a gear icon in the macOS status bar and lets you pick integrated only, discrete only, or dynamic switching for the GPU. Integrated only is meant to keep the discrete card idle so the battery lasts longer and to avoid buggy discrete drivers. The menu shows which GPU is currently active, and the icon shows a dot when the discrete GPU is in use. An optional notification fires when the active GPU changes, and it is off by default. The app can also be launched from the terminal with --integrated, --discrete, or --dynamic flags. The README notes that a display plugged in may force the discrete GPU and switch the app back to dynamic mode.
use_cases: Extend battery life on a dual-GPU MacBook Pro
Stop the discrete GPU from waking when it is not needed
Work around glitchy discrete GPU drivers
Switch GPU mode from the terminal or a script
Check which GPU is currently active
how_to_run: Download the latest release .zip, unzip it, and move gSwitch.app to the Applications folder
carthage bootstrap (run in the project folder)
notable: Menu bar gear icon with a dot that shows when the discrete GPU is active
Warns on dependent and hungry processes that use or want the discrete GPU
Optional notifications on GPU change, off by default
caveats: Archived: no further development or support; the author has not looked at it in about 5 years
Not useful on Apple Silicon MacBook Pros, which have no discrete GPU; the last model with one shipped in 2019
Does not work on MacBooks older than 2011 per the README, and requires macOS 10.12 or later
Cannot fully disable the discrete GPU; the OS can still access it briefly, and the README advises against attempts to disable it
